SUBTASK 25-21-71-010-010
(3) For the entry panel [2] that is part of the FWD lowered ceiling, do these steps to get access
through the entry light (if the light is not already open):
(a) Unlock the two 1/4-turn fasteners for the light bezel (at the right hand side of the light).
(b) Lower the right side of the bezel down and disconnect the lanyard.
(c) Continue to lower the right side of the bezel until you can disengage the spring clips on
the left side. Remove the bezel.
(d) Unlock the two 1/4-turn fasteners in the light housing. There is one on each side of the
light, near the forward end of the housing.
(e) Lower the forward edge of the entry light housing and disconnect the lanyard.
(f) Fully lower the forward edge of the light housing.
(g) Disconnect the electrical connector for the light.
(h) Remove the light housing. To remove it, lift it up a small amount and move it forward.

E. FWD Cove Bullnose Panel Removal
SUBTASK 25-21-71-010-038
(1) If necessary, do these steps to open the cove dome panel that is in the adjacent horseshoe
panel assembly:
(a) Find the two access holes in the space between the cove bull nose panel assembly [1]
and the horseshoe panel assembly.
(b) Put a 1/8 inch allen wrench, STD-15030, through the access holes.
(c) Turn the 1/8 inch allen wrench, STD-15030, 90°arc (2 rad) counterclockwise to release
the latches.
NOTE: This will let the cove dome panel open a small distance.
(d) Disconnect the lanyard.
(e) Open the cove dome panel fully.
SUBTASK 25-21-71-020-080
(2) Disconnect the electrical connector [14] above the cove bull nose panel assembly [1].
(a) Install a cap on the electrical connector [14] to prevent contamination.
SUBTASK 25-21-71-020-081
CAUTION
DO NOT SCRATCH OR HIT THE CEILING PANELS WHEN YOU REMOVE OR
INSTALL THEM. YOU CAN EASILY CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CEILING
PANELS.
(3) Do these steps to remove the FWD cove bull nose panel assembly [1].
(a) Remove the screws [16] and washers [17] from the bracket assemblies [12].
(b) Remove the screws [16] and washers [17] from the bracket assemblies [13].
(c) Remove the screws [18] and washers [19] from the bracket assemblies [11].
(d) Turn the cove bull nose panel assembly [1] out of its position.
(e) Remove the cove bull nose panel assembly [1].

1) Do not tighten the screws [18] at this time.

screws [16].

NOTE: Figure 401
A. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.

Opt Part #: J25008-1 Supplier: 81205

Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage

SUBTASK 25-22-00-860-006
(1) Open the applicable circuit breakers and attach DO-NOT-CLOSE tags for the electrical
equipment, if installed.
SUBTASK 25-22-00-020-001
(2) Remove the covers on the front and rear seat tracks.
SUBTASK 25-22-00-860-002

ALL

track fittings with the holes in the seat tracks.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

SUBTASK 25-22-00-210-002
(1) Do a visual check to make sure the seat belts are not worn, frayed, or damaged.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-22-00-980-001
(1) Make sure the passenger seats that are forward and aft of all the emergency exits do not
breakover into the pathways of the emergency exits.
NOTE: The Interior Configuration Specification for your airplanes should show requirements
for the emergency exit aisles. This is only applicable to airplanes that have seat
breakover.

Figure 601
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
231 Forward Passenger Compartment - Forward Entry Door to Sta 663.75 - Left
232 Forward Passenger Compartment - Forward Entry Door to Sta 663.75 - Right
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-22-00-211-001
(1) Make sure that the passenger seats that are in the area of the emergency exit doors do not
recline into the emergency exist aisles as defined by these dimensions.
(a) The minimum dimension of the emergency exit aisle for a triple seat is 13 in. (33 cm).
(b) The minimum dimension of the emergency exit aisle for a double seat is 6 in. (15.2 cm).

C. Track-mounted Passenger Seat Inspection
SUBTASK 25-22-00-200-009
(1) Make sure that the seat track fittings are installed correctly.
SUBTASK 25-22-00-200-010
(2) Hold the seat leg and try to move the seat forward and aft.
(a) The seat assembly must not move at the seat track fittings.
SUBTASK 25-22-00-010-004
(3) If the seat moves, do these steps:
(a) Remove the seat track covers.
(b) Tighten the rear seat track fitting to the recommended torque (TASK 25-22-00-400-802).
(c) Tighten the forward anti-rattle device manually plus 1/4 turn.
1) If there is no anti-rattle, tighten front fitting to the recommended torque
(TASK 25-22-00-400-802).
(d) Install the seat track covers.

Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-002
(1) Lower the adjacent spacer panel or PSU.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-003

5. Three-piece Adjustable PSU Spacer Panel Installation
(Figure 201)
A. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
G50532 T ape - Silicone, Foam BMS1-68
25-23-61
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-006
(1) Adjust the panel to the necessary width.
NOTE: This can be done while you hold the panel slider and push or pull on the panel base.
Repeat this to adjust the other panel base. Use the raised numbers on the slider panel
to get the correct width adjustment.
NOTE: You can apply some flexible foam tape, G50532 between the adjustable panels. This
is to increase the friction between the latch and rail, and keep the adjustable portion of
the spacer panel in position.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-007
(2) Put the index springs into the air outlet extrusion holes.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-008
(3) Push the inboard edge of the spacer panel outboard and upward until the cam latches engage
the bin rail.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-009
(4) Push the panel bases apart to close any gaps with the adjacent panels.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-010
(5) Apply upward pressure to the panel base under the cam latches to fully engage the latches.
NOTE: The latches will generally make a "click" sound when they fully engage.

(1) A termination panel is one which is against the stowage bin end cap.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-23-61-010-004
(1) Lower the panel adjacent to the panel slider side of the spacer panel until the spring clips no
longer grasp the adjacent panel wall.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-020-005
(2) Push the latch extensions of the cam latches and pull downward on the panel base until the
latches disengage from the bin rail.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-020-006
(3) Pull the corner spring coil inboard while you lower the inboard edge of the spacer panel.
(a) Pull the spacer panel inboard to remove the index springs from air outlet extrusion.

7. Two-piece Adjustable PSU Panel Installation
(Figure 201)
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-011
(1) Adjust the panel to the necessary width.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-012
(2) Lower the adjacent panel but do not remove it from the air outlet extrusion.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-013
(3) Locate the index springs into the holes of the air outlet extrusion.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-420-014

together until the cam latches engage the bin rail.

NOTE: The latches will generally make a "click" sound when they fully engage.

(Figure 201)
A. Location Zones
Zone Area

B. PSU Adjustment
SUBTASK 25-23-61-820-002
(1) To adjust the Passenger Service Unit (PSU), do these steps:
(a) Lower the PSU and adjacent spacer panels.
(b) Disengage the index pin on the support clamp from the index hole on the air conditioning
extrusion.
(c) Move the outboard support clamps and the PSU forward or aft to install the PSU in the
necessary position.
25-23-61
(d) Engage the index pin on the support clamp with the index hole in the air conditioning
extrusion.
NOTE: The forward edge of the PSU is ideally 18 in. (46 cm) forward of the cushion
reference point. The cushion reference point is where the seat back intersects
the seat cushion.
CAUTION
PUT THE WIRE BUNDLE AND GASPER HOSE BRACKET 7 1/2 +/-4
INCHES FORWARD OF THE AFT EDGE OF THE PSU PANEL. THE
BRACKET WILL CUT THE OXYGEN HOSE IF YOU PUT IT ADJACENT TO
THE OXYGEN GENERATOR. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(e) Attach the wire-bundle/gasper-hose bracket 3.5 in. (8.9 cm) to 11.5 in. (29.2 cm) forward
of the aft edge of the PSU panel, between the outboard latches.
(f) Make sure that the PSU is free to move when the unit is in the closed position.
1) Make sure that the cold air hose does not have any kinks or excessive bends.
(g) If it is necessary, move the wire bundle, or the cold air hose to a new outlet along the
side-wall.
(h) Lift the adjacent spacer panels.
1) Close the PSU.
SUBTASK 25-23-61-820-003
(2) Push the applicable spacer panel base forward or aft as required to close the gaps between
the panels.

the header assembly [1].

BE CAREFUL WITH THE HEADER ASSEMBLY . THE HEADER ASSEMBLY
CAN BECOME DAMAGED AND DIRTY EASILY .

clevis [11] to the top of the stowage bin.

SUBTASK 25-24-10-420-001

(a) If the class divider was moved to a new location, attach the support clevis [11] to the top
of the stowage bin, do these steps:

bins.
2) Install the nuts [12] that attach the support clevis [11] to the studs on the stowage
bins.
(b) Put the header assembly [1] in its position.

fittings on the support clevis [11].

support clevis [11].

the nut.

Figure 401):
1) Install the quick release pin [13] on the each end of the header assembly [1] to the
support clevis [11].

25-24-31-440-801Bin Assist Mechanism - ActivationPDF p. 525

2. Bin Assist Mechanism - Activation
Figure 201
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions to activate the bin assist mechanism.
B. Activate the Bin Assist Mechanism
SUBTASK 25-24-31-440-001
(1) To activate the bin assist mechanism, do these steps:
(a) Turn the inboard edge of the bin bucket up 1.5 in. (38.1 mm) or 3°arc (0 rad) minimum.
NOTE: The bearing must clear the cam bracket which is not visible with the installed
bucket. Turn the bin bucket more than 1.5 in. (38.1 mm) for the bearing to clear
the cam bracket.
(b) Use a hex wrench to tighten the bin assist screw. Tighten 20 in-lb (2 N·m) to 23 in-lb
(3 N·m).
NOTE: The head of the screw will be 0.33 in. (8.38 mm) from the outer edge of the cover
plate when correctly installed.
(c) Push the assist mechanism lever.
NOTE: The assist will not activate until load is applied to the bucket.
(d) Pull down on the threshold to apply load.
1) The bin assist will activate and start to pull the bin closed.
2) When assist is detected reapply load to threshold.
3) At the fully open position there should be two audible clicks.
NOTE: The assist is now reset.
(e) The assist mechanism lever will be in it's original position.
NOTE: The bin bucket will turn freely, open and closed, without activation of the assist.

7. Overhead Stowage Bin - Alternate Open Method
A. General
(1) This task opens the overhead stowage bin with a malfunctioning latch.
25-24-31
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-1641 Lever - Stowage Bin Release
Part #: J25001-5 Supplier: 81205
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-24-31-820-003
(1) If you can not open the stowage bin with the stowage bin handle, then do these steps to move
the emergency release lever to release the stowage bin latch.
NOTE: Usually the stowage bin handle will release one of the two latches. Use the emergency
release lever to release the other latch. Pull down lightly at each end of the stowage
bin, while you pull on the handle, to find which end is not released.
Procedure 1 (Using the lever, SPL-1641)
(a) Put the lever, SPL-1641 between the stowage bins above the latch.
NOTE: Two to three inches below the top edge of the stowage bin is a good location to
start.
NOTE: The lever, SPL-1641 should work at all latch locations, but it is a tight fit at the
slip joint locations. If you use it at a slip joint be careful not to damage the seal
(make sure the lever, SPL-1641 does not have sharp edges).
(b) Turn the lever, SPL-1641 to point toward the stowage bin you want to open.
(c) Move the lever, SPL-1641 down and outboard, keeping it in contact with the lip of the
stowage bin. At the same time, pull on the stowage bin handle (to release the other latch)
and pull down on the stowage bin to open it.
NOTE: You will feel the lever, SPL-1641 hit the emergency release lever. Push on the
lever, SPL-1641 until the latch opens.
NOTE: You must hold the emergency release lever until you open the bin. Usually the
latch will close again if you release the emergency release lever before you open
the bin.
(d) Procedure 2 (When the lever, SPL-1641, is not available)
NOTE: If the lever, SPL-1641, is available use it. It is the easier way to open the bin.
1) Open the stowage bin that is adjacent to the latch that will not release.
NOTE: If you cannot open a stowage bin adjacent to the latch you want to release
then you cannot use this procedure. You must use Procedure 1 above that
uses the lever, SPL-1641.
25-24-31
2) Put your finger (not all fingers will fit) or a small object (such as a 1/4 inch drive
deep socket or a Chapstick) in the channel at the edge of the stowage bin. Move it
down the channel behind the latch and push down on the emergency release lever
with it. At the same time, pull on the stowage bin handle (to release the other latch)
and pull down on the stowage bin to open it.
NOTE: You must hold the emergency release lever until you open the bin. Usually
the latch will close again if you release the emergency release lever before
you open the bin.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-820-004
(2) Replace or adjust latch if it is necessary.

2. Torque Tube Cover Doubler
(Figure 801)
A. General
(1) This task has the instructions for overhead stowage bin torque tube cover doubler installation.
(2) The 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) thick aluminum torque tube cover doubler strengthens and prevents
damage to the composite torque tube cover.
B. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
A50038 Adhesive - Fast-setting, 2 Part Epoxy, Medium
Viscosity
BMS5-123 Type I Class
2 Clear
B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735
B50201 Wipe - Alcohol (Isopropyl Alcohol)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
D. Repair Procedure
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-001
(1) Remove the screws adjacent to the worn area along the full length of the bin.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-002
(2) Install the torque tube cover and make sure that the holes in the doubler align with the bin
inserts.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-003
(3) OPTIONAL: Clean the torque tube and doubler faying surfaces with alcohol wipes, B50201 or
alcohol, B00130 then wipe dry before solvent evaporates.
NOTE: Avoid the use of ketones.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-004
(4) OPTIONAL: Prepare the adhesive, A50038, mixing gun, and a new dispensing tip. Make sure
that this mixes smoothly.
NOTE: The adhesive, A50038 is a fast setting epoxy with the pot life of 4 minutes.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-005
(5) OPTIONAL: Apply the 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) adhesive bead in two places at the underside of
the concave cross-section and outboard side angle.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-006
(6) Make sure that the torque tube cover doubler is installed correctly over the torque tube cover.
25-24-31
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-007
(7) OPTIONAL: Use masking tape (3M or equivalent) on the doubler whilst the adhesive cures.
Make sure that the tape is perpendicular to the doubler at equivalent distances along the
length.
NOTE: Make sure that only sufficient pressure is applied to hold the surfaces together.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-008
(8) Install the screws (BACS12FA3K5) and torque to 15 in-lb (1.7 N·m).
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-009
(9) OPTIONAL: Clean unwanted adhesive from the surfaces with alcohol wipes, B50201 or,
alcohol, B00130 and a clean wiper.
SUBTASK 25-24-31-350-010
(10) OPTIONAL: Make sure that the adhesive cures for 20-40 minutes before you remove the
masking tape. 50% cure strength in 1 hour, 100% cure strength in 24 hours.

SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-007
WARNING
CLEANING SOLVENT IS COMBUSTIBLE AND VAPOR MAY BE TOXIC. AVOID
PROLONGED BREATHING OF VAPOR AND PROLONGED OR REPEATED
CONTACT WITH SKIN. AVOID CONTACT WITH EYES. CLEAN PARTS IN

25-25-11
378-999 (Continued)
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
OBSERVE PRECAUTIONS FOR HANDLING ELECTROSTATIC SENSITIVE
DEVICES (ESD).
(1) Do these tasks to install the flipguard damper [3]:
(a) Clean the area with alcohol, B00130, and a cotton wiper, G00034.
1) Let it dry for 15 minutes.
(b) Apply a PR 1200 prime coat adhesion promoter, C00048 with a brush, G02439.
1) Let it dry for 15 minutes.
2) Wipe off the excess primer.
(c) Apply the adhesive, C00047, in the housing cavity.
(d) Install the flipguard damper [3] in the housing cavity over the adhesive and compress the
flipguard damper [3] in place with a cotton swab, G01659.
1) Wipe off the excess adhesive around the flipguard damper [3] with a clean cotton
swab, G01659.
a) Let it dry for 1 hour at 131°F (55°C) or air dry for 24 hours.
SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-008
(2) Do these tasks to prepare the flipguard assembly:
NOTE: The flipguard assembly consists of the flipguard [4] and the torsion springs [5].
(a) Insert one torsion spring [5] in the flipguard [4] with long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View
A1, Figure 403).
(b) Hold the torsion spring [5] with your thumb and remove the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733.
(c) Adjust the torsion spring [5] into place with the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View A1,
Figure 403).
(d) Insert a No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, halfway into the flipguard [4] to seal the torsion
spring [5] into place.
(e) Adjust the torsion spring [5] with the long-nosed pliers, STD-3733 (View A2, Figure 403).
(f) Insert the second torsion spring [5] into the flipguard [4].
(g) Insert the No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, all the way into the flipguard [4] to seal the second
torsion spring [5] into place (View A3, Figure 403).
SUBTASK 25-25-11-420-009
(3) Do these tasks to install the flipguard assembly:
NOTE: The flipguard assembly consists of the flipguard [4] and the torsion springs [5].
(a) Apply masking tape, G50314, on the housing to protect the surface of the housing.
(b) Position the flipguard assembly on the housing (View A4, Figure 403).
1) Insert the torsion springs [5] into the housing holes. If necessary, adjust the torsion
springs [5] into place with long-nosed pliers, STD-3733.
(c) Insert the flipguard screw [1] into the housing and the flipguard assembly (View A5,
Figure 403).
25-25-11
378-999 (Continued)
1) Use the screw [1] to push the No. 54 drill rod, STD-21008, out from the flipguard
assembly.
(d) Use a brush, G02439, to apply Loctite 425 adhesive, A50571, on the two outside threads
of the flipguard screw [1].
(e) Install the flipguard nut [2] on the flipguard screw [1].
1) Use a hex wrench, STD-7012, or 1/8 inch socket, STD-20883, to tighten the nut [2]
to 1.80 in-lb (0.20 N·m).
a) Use a second hex wrench, STD-7012, or 1/8 inch socket, STD-20883, to
prevent the screw [1] from turning.
SUBTASK 25-25-11-210-001
(4) Make sure that when you open and release the flipguard [4], it springs back to the closed

25-25-12-000-801Attendants' Seat RemovalPDF p. 623

2. Attendants' Seat Removal
(Figure 401)
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Attendants' Seat Removal
SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-001
(1) Remove the Headrest [4]. To remove it, pull on it. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners
(Velcro).
(a) Remove the mounting Bolts [5] and Washers [8] that attach the inertia reel bracket of the
seat belt to the wall.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-002
(2) Open the storage compartment door below the seat and remove the mounting Bolts [2] and
Washers [6].
SUBTASK 25-25-12-010-001
(3) Do these steps to open the lower seat back:
(a) Open the seat pan a small distance.
(b) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back. To
open it, pull it away from the upper seat back. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners
(Velcro).
(c) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back.
(d) Pull the seat back out and down.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-003
(4) Remove the mounting Bolts [3] and Washers [7] that are behind the lower seat back.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-020-004
(5) Remove the Attendant seat [1].
SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-001
(6) If installed, remove life vest located in the life vest container.
NOTE: N/A this step if seat is not being transported offsite. (This includes any mode of
transportation)
SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-002
(7) Route Attendant seat [1] to shop if necessary.
25-25-12-400-801Attendants' Seat InstallationPDF p. 624
Open original AMM PDF - page 624 ↗ 
3. Attendants' Seat Installation
(Figure 401)
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Attendants' Seat Installation
SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-001
(1) Put the Attendant seat [1] in its position.
(a) If the stowage box of the Attendant seat [1] has a cut-out, make sure that the cut-out is on
the outboard side.
NOTE: The cut-out provides additional clearance for the girt bar of the adjacent entry
door.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-002
(2) Open the storage compartment door below the seat and install the mounting Bolts [2] and
Washers [6].
SUBTASK 25-25-12-010-002
(3) Do these steps to open the lower seat back:
(a) Open the seat pan a small distance.
(b) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back. To
open it, pull it away from the upper seat back. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners
(Velcro).
(c) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back.
(d) Pull the seat back out and down.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-003
(4) Install the mounting Bolts [3] and Washers [7] that go behind the lower seat back.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-410-001
(5) Close the lower seat back.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-004
(6) Attach the inertia reel bracket of the seat belt to the wall with its Bolts [5] and Washers [8].
SUBTASK 25-25-12-420-005
(7) Install the Headrest [4]. It is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro).
SUBTASK 25-25-12-869-003
(8) If required for overwater operation, install one each life vest in life vest container.
25-25-12-200-801Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment InspectionPDF p. 627
Open original AMM PDF - page 627 ↗ 
2. Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment Inspection
(Figure 601)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
B. Attendants' Seat and Harness Attachment Inspection
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-001
(1) Make sure that the seat belts and the shoulder harness are not worn or damaged.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-002
(2) Do these steps to examine the top mounting bolts [5] of the seat:
(a) Remove the headrest [4].
NOTE: The headrest is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro).
1) To remove it, pull on the headrest [4].
(b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [5] that attach the bracket for the inertia reels to the
wall are not loose.
(c) Make sure that the mounting bolts that attach the inertia reels of the shoulder harness to
the bracket are not loose.
(d) Install the headrest.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-003
(3) Do these steps to examine the middle mounting bolts of the seat:
(a) Do these steps to open the lower seat back:
1) Open the seat pan a small distance.
2) Open the fabric flap that is between the lower seat back and the upper seat back.
NOTE: The fabric flap is attached with hook and loop fasteners (Velcro).
a) To open it, pull the fabric flap away from the upper seat back.
3) Push the two latches on the lower seat back toward the center of the seat back.
4) Pull the seat back out and down.
(b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [3] that attach the seat to the wall are not loose.
(c) Close the lower seat back.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-004
(4) Do these steps to examine the lower mounting bolts of the seat:
(a) Open the storage compartment door.
25-25-12
(b) Make sure that the mounting bolts [2] that attach the seat to the wall are not loose.
(c) Close the storage compartment door.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-005
(5) Do these steps to examine the lower attachment points for the seat belts:
(a) Pull the seat cushion away from the attachment points for the seat belts.
(b) Make sure that the bolts are tight.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-200-001
(6) Do these steps to inspect the pivot points of the seat pan:
(a) Open the seat pan.
(b) Hold the seat pan near its back corner and shake the seat pan to make sure that it is not
loose.
(c) Make sure that the seat pan has no obvious cracks.

(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task is an inspection of the attendants' seat bottom, referred to in this procedure as the
seat pan.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-25-12-710-001
(1) Push the seat pan fully down (open) and release it. Make sure the seat pan retracts to its fully
up (closed) position without aid.
SUBTASK 25-25-12-210-006
(2) Do these steps to examine the pivot points of the seat pan:
(a) Open the seat pan.
(b) Hold the seat pan near its back corner and shake the seat pan to make sure it is not
loose.
(c) Make sure the seat pan has no obvious cracks.

SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-006

SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-007
(2) Remove the entry and service area floor covering.
(a) Release the mat from the edge thresholds.
(b) If it is necessary, remove the sealant around the mat.
(c) Carefully release the mat from the tape that holds the mat to the waterseal.
25-27-21

1) Pull the strips of 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, or 3M 8663

2) Remove fillet seal from the edges of the sidewall.
F . Floor Covering Removal Alternate Method
SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-008
(1) Remove the entry area mat.
(a) Remove the fasteners from the doorway threshold and flight deck threshold.
(b) Remove the girt bar latch fittings (TASK 25-66-02-000-801).
(c) Remove or loosen the doorway threshold and flight deck threshold to release the mats.
CAUTION
OBEY THESE PRECAUTIONS. IF YOU IGNORE THESE
PRECAUTIONS, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT WILL OCCUR.
1) Be careful when you remove the mat; do not damage the waterseal when you use a
skin wedge, STD-1178, or equivalent.
(d) Remove the plastic aisle threshold with a skin wedge, STD-1178, or equivalent.
SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-009
(2) Do these steps, when entry and service area floor covering with monuments is installed:
(a) Separate the edge of the mat from the tape.
(b) If it is necessary, remove the sealant around the mat.
(c) Pull the mat upward from the tape and toward the monument wall.
NOTE: This area is where the mat will be trimmed.
(d) Put a protective strip fabric, G00088, or equivalent between the waterseal and mat.
NOTE: The waterseal can be damaged if the fabric, G00088, or equivalent is not used to
protect it.
(e) Carefully cut the mat that is adjacent to the monument walls.
NOTE: This is to start the mat removal.
(f) Release the rest of the mat.
(g) Carefully pull the mat from under the monument wall.
SUBTASK 25-27-21-000-010
(3) If you replace the entire area, do these steps to remove the waterseal:
(a) Pull the strips of 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, 3M 8663 tape,
G51482, or moisture barrier tape, G51340 from the floor.

(1) If the waterseal is not removed and replaced, prepare the waterseal surface for the mat.
(a) Examine the waterseal for cuts, tears abrasions, or other signs of deterioration.
(b) If it is necessary, repair the waterseal.
1) Do this task: Vinyl Water Barrier Repair, TASK 53-21-11-300-801 or Mylar Water
Barrier Repair, TASK 53-21-11-300-802.
2) Do this task: Repair the Polyurethane Waterseal, TASK 53-21-00-300-801.
(c) If it is necessary, clean the waterseal with oil-free cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with
Series 91 solvent, B01011.
(d) Clean the sealant from the edge thresholds.
1) Do not let the solvent get on the waterseal or on the undisturbed sealant.
SUBTASK 25-27-21-840-002
(2) If the waterseal is removed, prepare the floor panels for the waterseal.
(a) Clean the floor panels, do these steps:
1) Apply Series 91 solvent, B01011, with clean oil-free cotton wiper, G00034.
2) Rub the surface to remove the soil.
3) Use clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it
evaporates.
(b) Protect the floor tracks from corrosion (SRM 51-20-01).
(c) Keep the floor panels clean prior to applying the waterseal.
E. Floor Covering Installation
SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-001
(1) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the waterseal:
CAUTION
DO NOT CUT THE TAPE AGAINST A FLOOR PANEL, SEAT TRACK,
ATTACH FITTING, OR OTHER TAPE. CORROSION AND STRUCTURAL
DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE EQUIPMENT .
(a) Apply moisture barrier tape, G50179, to all floor panel seams in the galley and lavatory
areas, extending 20 in. (51 cm) aft of the forward wet area and 20 in. (51 cm) forward of
the aft wet area.
25-27-21
(b) Apply 3M 8663DL tape, G02500, 3M 8663 tape, G02423, 3M 8663 tape, G51482, or
moisture barrier tape, G51340, across the entire area perpendicular to the center line of
the airplane.
1) Make sure that there is a minimum of a 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) overlap of each strip.
(c) Push the tape down firmly in all areas.
(d) Apply sealant, A00247, or sealant, A02315, to the edges, cracks, and small holes.
1) Make sure that the waterseal and adjacent structure has a complete seal.
(e) Clean the surface of the waterseal with an cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series
91 solvent, B01011.
1) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it
evaporates.
F . Floor Covering Installation Standard Method
SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-006
(1) Install the entry area mat.
(a) Install the entry monuments as necessary.
NOTE: The galleys, lavatories, and partitions that edge the sides of the entry mat must
be installed before the mat.
(b) Cut the mat to the correct dimensions.
(c) Apply carpet tape, G01288, 6.0 in. (15.2 cm) wide, on the floor surface with no gaps.
NOTE: Avoid running the tape over the raised areas and floor panel inserts. The
direction of the tape is optional.
NOTE: Adhesive Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, has displayed better results in countering mat
buckling. Recommended to use this tape in areas of observed buckling.
NOTE: Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, has stronger adhesion properties making it more
difficult to remove, care should be taken in its removal.
1) Keep carpet tape, G01288, at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.50 in.
(12.70 mm) from the mat edges.
(d) Apply RTV6708 adhesive, A50030, for faying surfaces on the trim as well as sealing all
the cracks and small holes.
NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to RTV6708 adhesive, A50030.
(e) Clean the bottom side of the mat with an cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 91
solvent, B01011, that will contact the waterseal.
1) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove Series 91 solvent, B01011, before it
evaporates.
(f) Put the mat in the correct location and push firmly on the tape.
(g) Apply adhesive, A00930, at least 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) and no more than 0.35 in. (8.89 mm)
wide, between the edge of the mat and floor panel.
NOTE: adhesive, A00027, is optional to adhesive, A00930.
(h) Put the edges in the edge thresholds before the sealant starts to get hard.
SUBTASK 25-27-21-420-008
(2) Put the carpet in the edge threshold for the mats.

F . Galley Water Filter Replacement
SUBTASK 25-31-10-900-001
(1) Remove the water filter.
(a) Put a container, STD-193, or cotton cloth, G50316, below the filter case [3] to absorb
spilled water.
(b) Loosen the vent screw [6] (where applicable) and let the water drain from the pressure
vessel.
(c) Remove the clamp [5] at the top of the filter case [3].
25-31-10
(d) Remove the filter cartridge [4] from the filter case [3].
(e) If it is necessary, examine the cartridge seal and housing gasket.
NOTE: Contact the galley manufacturer for the part numbers of the seal or gaskets.
SUBTASK 25-31-10-960-001
(2) Replace the water filter.
(a) Clean the inner part of the filter case [3] with a clean cotton cloth, G50316.
(b) Install a clean filter cartridge [4].
1) Flush the new filter cartridge [4] at the time of installation.
NOTE: This is done by running water through the filter at full flow from the service
top for three minutes or until water runs clear.
(c) Install the clamp [5].
1) Make sure that the clamp [5] is installed in the correct position and head of the
wingnut does not cause the interference with the cart.
(d) Tighten the wingnut on the clamp [5].
(e) Open the water shutoff valve [2].
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-24-1147
(f) Set the GALLEY switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the ON position.
043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179,
182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341,
343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-24-1147
(g) Set the CAB/UTIL switch, on the P5 overhead panel, to the ON position.
ALL
(h) Open the vent screw [6] at the top of the filter case [3] to bleed air.
(i) Close the vent screw [6].
(j) Pressurize the potable water system.
1) Do this task: Potable Water System - Activation, TASK 38-42-00-800-802.
(k) Open the faucet.
(l) Make sure that there are no leaks around the water filter assembly [1].

G. Galley Installation
SUBTASK 25-31-11-210-001
(1) Do a check of the water barrier on the galley floor for damage.
(a) If it is necessary, do this task: Entry and Service Area Floor Covering - Installation,
TASK 25-27-21-400-801.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-100-001
(2) Clean the galley mat on the floor in the galley area with solvent, B00083.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-350-001
(3) If it is necessary, repair the galley mat.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-001
(4) Move the galley inboard near its final position.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-139
(5) Connect the ground strap [4] to the ground stud [3].
SUBTASK 25-31-11-760-003
(6) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the top of the galley and ground stud [3]
(SWPM 20-20-00).
(a) Use the non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
(b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 Ohms (2.5 milliohms) or less.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-007
(7) Connect the electrical connectors [8] in the ceiling above the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-017
(8) If exit light is installed, put the wires through the panel before the galley is in its final position.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-002
(9) Put the galley into its final position.
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343,
346-999
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-011
(10) If necessary, install the stabilizer [14].
(a) Put the stabilizer [14] below the galley.
(b) Attach the stabilizer [14] with the bolts [15] and washers [16].
1) Torque the bolts [15] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
(c) Seal the stabilizer [14] with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930.
ALL
25-31-11
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-012
(11) Connect the water supply.
(a) Connect the water supply connection [5] at the top of the galley.
(b) Install the shroud [6] on the water supply connection [5] with plastic tie straps [7].
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-003
(12) If it is necessary, loosely install the bolts [9], washers [10], and shims [11] at the four floor hard
points.
NOTE: This will prevent galley movement while the floor seals are installed.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-085
(13) If necessary, install the floor seals and bond them with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive,
A00930.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-004
(14) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [9] and install the bolts [9], washers [10], and shims [11]
at the four floor hard points.
NOTE: Install the shims as necessary. The shim installation could not be more than 3 shims
per attachment fitting.
(a) Tighten the bolts [9] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-005
(15) Install the hard point coverplates and seal with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-820-002
(16) Attach the tie rod [1] to the attachment fitting on the top of the galley.
(a) If it is necessary, adjust the tie rod [1] to the correct length.
1) Adjust only the end of the assembly without the lockwasher and lockwire.
NOTE: The end of the tie rod with the lockwasher and lockwire attached at the
fitting on the fuselage.
2) Make sure that the thread of the tie rod [1] blocks the inspection hole in the body of
the tie rod [1].
3) Tighten the jamnut.
(b) Install the quick release pin [2] at the galley end of the tie rod [1].
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-013
(17) If necessary, through the lower outboard access panel, connect the drain [12] and tighten the
clamp.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-008
(18) Through the applicable lower outboard access panel, connect the door flexible duct [13] and
tighten the clamp.
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-009
(19) If necessary, install the light assembly for the floor proximity light (TASK 33-51-14-960-802).
SUBTASK 25-31-11-420-134
(20) If it is removed, install the exit sign light assembly (Exit Sign Light Assembly Replacement,
TASK 33-51-01-960-802).
SUBTASK 25-31-11-390-001
(21) Apply a 0.25 in. (0.64 cm) - 0.35 in. (0.89 cm) fillet seal between the mat and galley with
adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930.

F . Galley Removal
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-013
(1) Disconnect the water supply at the connection at the top of the galley.
(a) Get access through the applicable access panel in the top of the galley.
(b) Disconnect the water connection [4] above the top of the galley.
25-31-21
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-004
(2) Through the lower access panel, loosen the clamp [5], then disconnect the drain line [6].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-005
(3) Remove the tie rod [9].
(a) Remove the quick-release pin [10] that attaches the tie rod [9] to the galley lug fitting [11].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-006
(4) To remove the galley floor hard points, do these steps:
(a) Remove the coverplate on the floor hard points.
(b) If it is necessary, remove the grease from the attachment fitting to get access to the
fasteners.
(c) Remove the bolts [12], washers [13], and shims [14] at the four hard point locations.
NOTE: Keep the shims for the galley installation. Record the quantity of shims for a
given location when you remove the shims.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-009
(5) Do these steps to remove the stabilizer [21] fitting:
(a) Remove the bolts [15], washers [16], and nuts [17] at the bearing block [18].
(b) Remove the bearing block [18].
(c) Remove the bolts [19] and washers [20] at the stabilizer [21].
(d) Remove the stabilizer [21].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-042
(6) If it is necessary, move the galley out slightly for easier access to the electrical connectors [1]
and ground stud [3].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-011
(7) Disconnect the electrical power at the connections above the galley.
(a) Disconnect the electrical connectors [1].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-012
(8) Disconnect the ground strap [2] from the ground stud [3] at the top of the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-020-010
(9) Lift up and remove the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-030-002
(10) If it is necessary, remove the seat track fittings at the seat track locations.

F . Galley Installation
SUBTASK 25-31-21-210-001
(1) Do a check of the water barrier on the galley floor for damage.
(a) If it is necessary do this task: Entry and Service Area Floor Covering - Installation,
TASK 25-27-21-400-801.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-100-001
(2) Clean the galley mat on the floor in the galley area with solvent, B00083.
25-31-21
SUBTASK 25-31-21-350-001
(3) If it is necessary, repair the galley mat.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-023
(4) If it is necessary, install the seat track fittings at the seat track locations.
(a) Do this task: Seat Track Filler Application, TASK 51-21-92-600-801.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-001
(5) Move the galley inboard.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-095
(6) Connect the galley ground strap [2] to the galley ground stud [3].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-760-003
(7) Do a resistance check of the static ground from the ground stud [3] on the galley to the
airplane ground stud.
(a) Make sure that the resistance is a maximum of 0.0025 ohm (2.5 miliohms).
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-008
(8) Connect the electrical connectors [1] in the ceiling above the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-820-001
(9) If it is necessary, adjust the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-002
(10) Lift and put the galley into its correct position.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-027
(11) If it is necessary, loosely install the bolts [12], washers [13], and shims [14] at the four hard
points.
NOTE: This will prevent galley movement while the floor seals are installed.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-003
(12) Install the floor seals and bond them with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-026
(13) Install the bolts [12], washers [13], and shims [14] at the floor hard points.
NOTE: Install the shims as necessary. The shim installation may not be more than 3 shims per
attachment fitting.
(a) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [12].
(b) Torque the bolts [12] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-005
(14) Install the hard point coverplates and seal with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-006
(15) Do these steps to install the stabilizer [21]:
(a) Put the stabilizer [21] below the galley.
(b) Install the bolts [19] and washers [20] at the stabilizer [21].
1) Torque the bolts [19] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
(c) Install the bearing block [18] on the stabilizer [21].
(d) Install the bolts [15], washers [16], and nuts [17] at the bearing block [18].
(e) Seal the stabilizer with adhesive, A00930.
25-31-21
SUBTASK 25-31-21-820-002
(16) Do these steps to attach the tie rod [9] to the lug fitting [11] on the galley:
(a) Adjust the tie rod [9] to the correct length.
1) Adjust only the end of the assembly without the lockwasher and the lockwire.
2) Make sure that the thread of the tie rod blocks the inspection hole in the body of the
tie rod.
3) Tighten the jamnut.
(b) Install the quick-release pin [10] at the galley end of the tie rod [9].
1) Install the end of the tie rod [9] with the lockwasher and the lockwire at the fitting on
the fuselage.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-009
(17) If applicable, connect the water connection [4] at the top of the galley.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-010
(18) If applicable, through the lower outboard access panel, connect the drain line [6] and tighten
the clamp [5].
SUBTASK 25-31-21-390-001
(19) Apply a fillet seal between the mat and galley wall with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive,
A00930.
SUBTASK 25-31-21-420-028
(20) Do this task: Lowered Ceiling Installation, TASK 25-21-71-400-801 or Lowered Ceiling
Installation, TASK 25-21-71-400-815.

C. Sealant Installation Procedure
SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-001
(1) FOR LAVATORIES WITH BI-FOLD DOORS;
Do these steps to apply sealant to the threshold area:
(a) Remove the bi-fold door [5].
(b) If necessary, remove the threshold [2] installed bellow the lavatory [1] door.
(c) Clean the areas that will be sealed (TASK 51-31-00-160-801).
(d) Apply a bead of sealant [3] of RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 around the bi-fold door pivot
hole [11] (TASK 51-31-00-390-801).
(e) Install the threshold [2].
(f) Remove the excess RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 from the threshold [2].
(g) Apply a sealant [4] around the interior edges of the threshold [2] with RTV 108 adhesive,
A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
(h) Install the bi-fold door [5].
SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-002
(2) FOR LAVATORIES WITHOUT BI-FOLD DOORS;
25-40-01
Do these steps to apply sealant to the threshold area:
(a) If necessary, remove the threshold [2] installed below the lavatory [1] door.
(b) Clean the areas that will be sealed (TASK 51-31-00-160-801).
(c) Install the threshold [2].
(d) Apply a sealant [4] around the interior edges of the threshold [2] with RTV 108 adhesive,
A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-003
(3) Apply sealant to the lavatory cover plates [6]:
(a) Apply fay surface sealant [7] to the cover plates [6] with adhesive, A00027, adhesive,
A00930 or RTV 108 adhesive, A00635 (TASK 51-31-00-390-801).
(b) Install the cover plates [6] to the lavatory foor fittings [8].
SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-004
(4) Install the new floor sealant [3] between panels and floor and the wall adjacent to the airplane
door.
(a) Clean the area where the sealant will be applied (TASK 51-31-00-160-801).
(b) Bond the floor seal with adhesive, A00027, or adhesive, A00930
(TASK 51-31-00-390-801).
NOTE: Seal on the wall panel seam must be continuous approximately 6 in. (152 mm)
from the floor.
SUBTASK 25-40-01-400-005
(5) Apply one of these sealants to all exposed fasteners, gaps, or seams less than 6 in.
(152.4 mm) up from the floor.
NOTE: Select the color to match the adjacent surfaces. It is possible to use RTV 108
adhesive, A00635, for all variations.
• RTV 102 adhesive, A50067
• RTV 103 adhesive, A50119
• RTV 106 adhesive, A00081
• RTV 108 adhesive, A00635
• RTV109 sealant, A50011.

2. Lavatory Waste Compartment Inspection
(Figure 601)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044
B. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044; LAVATORIES WITH AN INNER WASTE COMPARTMENT
DOOR
SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-001
(1) Do these steps for lavatories with an inner waste compartment door and an outer waste
compartment door to make sure the waste compartment doors close correctly:
(a) Open the outer waste compartment door.
(b) Open the inner waste compartment door and release it.
1) Make sure the springs close the inner door without your help.
(c) Make sure the inner door is not bent or blocked such that it does not close fully. It must
close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire.
(d) Close the outer waste compartment door.
1) Make sure the latch holds the outer door closed.
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044; LAVATORIES WITHOUT AN INNER WASTE
COMPARTMENT DOOR
SUBTASK 25-40-08-800-001
(2) Do these steps for lavatories that do not have an inner waste compartment door to make sure
the outer waste compartment door closes correctly.
(a) Open the waste compartment door.
(b) Make sure the door and seals are not damaged or blocked so that it does not fully close.
NOTE: The door must closely tightly to make sure that it can contain a fire.
NOTE: Some doors have a door plate with springs behind it instead of a visible seal.
(c) Close the waste compartment door.
(d) Make sure the waste compartment door latches correctly and holds the door securely
closed.
25-40-08
056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203,
205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-416
C. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure
SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-003
(1) Do these steps to make sure the door closes tightly:
(a) Pull the latch at the bottom of the door to open the door.
(b) Push around the edge of the door plate on the inner side of the door.
1) Make sure the door plate moves quickly back to its initial position.
NOTE: There are springs behind the door plate. These springs compress when the
door is closed.
(c) Do a visual check of the door plate on the inner side of the door for general condition.
(d) Close the door.
(e) Do these steps to make sure the latches are fully engaged:
1) Push the door in the upper and lower latch area.
2) Make sure the lower latch is parallel to the door.
NOTE: If you can easily see red on the lower latch, the latches are not fully
engaged.
417-999
D. Waste Compartment Door Inspection Procedure
SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-004
(1) Do these steps for lavatories with an inner waste compartment door and an outer waste
compartment door to make sure the waste compartment doors close correctly:
(a) Open the outer waste compartment door.
NOTE: The latch is at the bottom of the door.
(b) Open the inner waste compartment door and release it.
1) Make sure that the springs close the inner door without your help.
(c) Make sure the inner door is not bent or blocked such that it does not close fully. It must
close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire.
(d) Close the outer waste compartment door.
1) Make sure the latch holds the outer door closed.
ALL
E. Waste Compartment Flap Inspection Procedure
SUBTASK 25-40-08-210-002
(1) Do these steps to make sure the waste compartment flap operates correctly:
(a) Push the waste compartment flap open.
(b) Release the waste compartment flap and make sure it closes fully.
(c) Make sure the waste compartment flap is not bent such that it does not close fully. It must
close tightly to make sure it can contain a fire.

(BMS8-371) in pieces.
(e) Do these steps to wrap insulation tape around the insulation foam on the water supply
line:

foam, G50408 (BMS8-371).

insulation foam, G50408 (BMS8-371), begins.
3) Continue to wind the insulation tape, G50327 (BMS5-157), or tape, G51202, around
the insulation foam, G50408 (BMS8-371), with a 0.2 +0.3 / -0.0 in.
(5.1 +7.6 / -0.0 mm) overlap for each turn, and stop after the insulation foam,

seals over the ends of the insulation foam, G50408 (BMS8-371), fully.

show.

2. Forward Cargo Compartment Liner Inspection
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task inspects all the liners in the forward cargo compartment.
(2) It is important that all of the fasteners, seams, and punctures are sealed correctly to keep the
amount of oxygen in the compartment to a minimum.
B. References
Reference Title
21-32-05 P/B 401 CARGO COMPARTMENT BLOWOUT PANELS -
REMOVAL/INSTALLATION
25-00-00-300-801 Crushed-Core and Sandwich Panel Repair (P/B 801)
25-52-01-300-802 Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with
Complex Curves (P/B 801)
25-52-01-300-806 Neoprene Coated Cargo Liner Repair (P/B 801)
25-52-01-300-807 Silicone Impregnated Liner Repair (P/B 801)
25-52-01-300-808 Permanent Repair for the Contour of the Ceiling Shroud
(P/B 801)
25-52-01-340-801 Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners (P/B 801)
25-52-01-350-801 Loose or Damaged T ape Repair (P/B 801)
25-52-06-000-801 Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal (P/B 401)
25-52-06-400-801 Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation (P/B 401)
25-52-09-000-801 Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal (P/B 401)
25-52-09-400-801 Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation (P/B 401)
25-52-10-000-801 Cargo Floor Panel - Removal (P/B 401)
25-52-10-400-801 Cargo Floor Panel - Installation (P/B 401)
25-52-16-000-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner -
Removal (P/B 401)
25-52-16-400-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner -
Installation (P/B 401)
25-52-17-000-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal
(P/B 401)
25-52-17-400-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation
(P/B 401)
25-52-00
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
121 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left
122 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-001
(1) Make sure that there is no loose or damaged tape at the joints for the ceiling liner, sidewall
liner or bulkhead liner.
(a) If there is loose or damaged tape, replace the tape (TASK 25-52-01-350-801).
SUBTASK 25-52-00-211-001
(2) Make sure that the ceiling liners, sidewall liners, bulkhead liners and panels, blowout panels
and floor panels do not have any cuts, tears, cracks, or holes.
(a) If there are cuts, tears, cracks or holes found on the blowout panel, replace the blowout
panel (PAGEBLOCK 21-32-05/401).
SUBTASK 25-52-00-200-006
(3) If damage is found, examine the non-honeycomb liners for damage as follows:
NOTE: These damage limits apply to all the non-honeycomb liners. These are the ceiling
panels and shrouds, sidewall, forward bulkhead and aft cargo compartment liners.
These damage limits do not apply to cracks along the contour of the ceiling shroud in
the forward cargo compartment.
(a) Cuts that are longer than 36 in. (91 cm) are not repairable.
(b) L-shaped tears that are longer than 9 in. (23 cm) on either side are not repairable.
(c) Holes that are over 1.5 in. (3.8 cm) in diameter are not repairable.
(d) Cracks within 2 in. (5 cm) of other damage, or from any panel edge are not repairable.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-006
(4) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do the applicable task to repair the liner:
(a) Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners, TASK 25-52-01-340-801.
(b) Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves,
TASK 25-52-01-300-802.
NOTE: T ask Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex
Curves, TASK 25-52-01-300-802 for cracks along the contour of the ceiling
shroud. This can be the ceiling shroud in the forward cargo compartment or other
areas with contours.
(c) Neoprene Coated Cargo Liner Repair, TASK 25-52-01-300-806.
(d) Silicone Impregnated Liner Repair, TASK 25-52-01-300-807.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-007
(5) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the applicable liner as follows:
(a) Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801 and Cargo
Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-09-400-801.
(b) Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal, TASK 25-52-06-000-801 and Cargo
Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation, TASK 25-52-06-400-801.
(c) Cargo Floor Panel - Removal, TASK 25-52-10-000-801 and Cargo Floor Panel -
Installation, TASK 25-52-10-400-801.
25-52-00
SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-007
(6) If damage is found, examine the contour of the ceiling shroud in the cargo compartment for
damage as follows:
(a) Make sure that cracks are at least 2 in. (5 cm) away from other damage and from the
panel edge on all sides.
NOTE: These damage limits only apply to cracks or cuts along the bend of the shroud. For
damage to the flat parts of the shroud, use the damage limits and repair instructions
for non-honeycomb liners.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-002
(7) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do this task to repair the lining:
(a) Permanent Repair for the Contour of the Ceiling Shroud, TASK 25-52-01-300-808.
(b) Permanent Repair for Molded Liners, Shrouds, and Liners with Complex Curves,
TASK 25-52-01-300-802.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-003
(8) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the liner (Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner -
Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801 and Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation,
TASK 25-52-09-400-801).
SUBTASK 25-52-00-200-005
(9) If damage is found, examine the nomex honeycomb panels for damage as follows:
(a) For panels with core damage, there must be at least 0.5 in. (1.3 cm) of undamaged core
around the damaged area.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-300-003
(10) If the damage is less than or equal to the limits, do the following steps:
NOTE: Dents on the cargo compartment bulkhead panel assembly that shows no damage to
the integrity of the facesheet (e.g. holes, cracks, damaged fiber) are structurally
acceptable and repair is not necessary.
(a) Do this task: Crushed-Core and Sandwich Panel Repair, TASK 25-00-00-300-801.
(b) Apply a flame-resistant patch (Permanent Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners,
TASK 25-52-01-340-801).
NOTE: Multiple damage sites may be covered with longer strips in lieu of multiple shorter
strips.
NOTE: Patch may be applied over fastener locations by removing the fastener and
reinstalling through the patch.
NOTE: Splices in the patch system require a minimum of one (1) inch overlap.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-960-004
(11) If the damage is greater than the limits, replace the applicable liner as follows:
(a) Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal,
TASK 25-52-16-000-801 and Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner -
Installation, TASK 25-52-16-400-801.
(b) Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-17-000-801 and
Forward Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-17-400-801.

3. Cargo Compartment Blowout Panel Inspection
A. References
Reference Title

B. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage
C. Blowout Panel Inspection
SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-006
(1) Make sure the blowout panel is fully engaged between the retaining ring and the rectangular
seal.
(a) Do these steps to put the blowout panel in the correct position if it is not fully engaged:
1) Remove the screws and washers that attach the grill to the frame.
2) Remove the grill.
3) Loosen the applicable bolts that attach the retaining ring to the frame in the area
where the blowout panel came out.
4) Make sure that the blowout panel do not have any cuts, tears, cracks, or holes.
a) If there are cuts, tears, cracks or holes found on the blowout panel, replace the
blowout panel (PAGEBLOCK 21-32-05/401).
5) Put the blowout panel in the position between the retaining ring and the rectangular
seal.
6) Tighten the bolts that attach the retaining ring to the frame.
7) Install the screws and washers to attach the grill to the frame.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-210-007
(2) Make sure the grill is firmly attached and is aft of the blowout panel.

CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PAINT OR CAN CAUSE THE CORROSION OF
METAL SURFACES
(4) Cover the areas that you will not clean. Use Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 with
one of the these protective materials:
NOTE: This includes protection of all the lubricated or waxed surfaces and the latches and
fittings.
• polyethylene film, G00252
• barrier material, G00253
• Angier 30 paper, G00258.
G. Clean the cargo compartment
SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-001
(1) Remove the dirt, fluids, and the other loose material with a high capacity vacuum, STD-1068
as necessary.
25-52-00
SUBTASK 25-52-00-110-002
WARNING
DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN.
DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A
PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE
MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND
HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
CAUTION
DO NOT USE SOLVENTS THAT ARE NOT ON THE LIST OF CONSUMABLE
MATERIALS. IF YOU USE OTHER SOLVENTS, DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT COULD OCCUR.
(2) Apply the solution of alkaline cleaner and water to the compartment with the airless pump,
STD-7824 or the Graco bulldog portable airless pump.
(a) Let the solution soak for 5 minutes, but do not let it dry.
(b) Apply more solution as necessary to keep the surfaces wet.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-002
(3) Remove the solution and the materials loosened by the solution with the high capacity
vacuum, STD-1068.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-003
(4) Do steps (2) and (3) again until the compartment is clean, as necessary.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-170-001
(5) Flush the compartment with clean water.
(a) Use pressure to apply the water.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-004
(6) Remove the water with the high capacity vacuum, STD-1068, as necessary.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-750-001
(7) Do this pH check for the compartment as follows with litmus paper, G50412:
(a) Do a pH check of the clean water.
(b) Do a pH check of the water which remains caught in the compartment.
1) Do this check in more than one area.
(c) Compare the pH check of the clean water with the pH of the water still caught in the
compartment.
(d) Make sure the pH in step (b) is not more than 1 pH unit of the pH in step (a).
1) If necessary, flush the compartment again with clean water.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-160-005
(8) Dry the area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-620-001
(9) Do this task: Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802.
H. Put the Airplane Back in its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 25-52-00-950-002
(1) Remove all of the masking tape and paper.
25-52-00
SUBTASK 25-52-00-410-001
(2) Install the equipment you removed.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-910-002
(3) Remove the static ground.
SUBTASK 25-52-00-860-002
(4) If it is necessary, do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.

A. General

1 Grade A

(Perchloroethylene)

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 25-52-01-020-003
(1) Remove or discard all loose or damaged tape.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-004
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE SOLVENT TOUCH PLASTICS, CONTROL CABLES,
LUBRICATED AREAS, PLASTIC DECALS, OR PAINTED AREAS OR
MARKINGS THAT ARE NOT SKYDROL RESISTANT . THE SOLVENT WILL
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE ITEMS.
(2) Clean the damaged area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00093,
or solvent, B00090.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-005
(3) Dry the area with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034, before the solvent dries.
25-52-01
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-006
(4) Clean the area again fully to remove the dirt, oil, paint, and other unwanted materials.
NOTE: A clean surface is necessary for a good bond.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-420-003
WARNING
DO NOT PUT TAPE ON THE SMOKE DETECTOR TUBES OR THE FIRE
EXTINGUISHER OUTLET TUBES. THE SMOKE DETECTOR AND THE FIRE
EXTINGUISHER SYSTEM WILL NOT SENSE A FIRE IF THERE IS TAPE ON
THE TUBE OR OUTLETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
WARNING
DO NOT APPLY TAPE ON THE BLOWOUT PANELS OR CAP STRIPS ON THE
CEILING LINER. IN THE AFT CARGO COMPARTMENT , DO NOT APPLY TAPE
BETWEEN THE CEILING LINER AND CAP STRIP ALONG THE CEILING
CENTERLINE. THE JOINT GIVES A VENT PATH FOR AIR FLOW IF A
DECOMPRESSION OCCURS. IF THE PRESSURE RELIEF FUNCTION
OPERATES INCORRECTLY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL,
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(5) Apply T ape, A50465, to the area.
NOTE: Apply the tape with the minimum number of joints in it. Do not apply tape between the
ceiling liner and aft bulkhead liner. The tape at this joint should be only on the ceiling
liner. In both the forward and aft cargo compartments, the aft bulkhead does not need
tape applied to its joints.
NOTE: Do not use the old tape again. If you use the tape again, it will not have a satisfactory
bond.
NOTE: Do not apply the tape to the blowout panels or cap strips on the ceiling liner.
NOTE: Do not apply tape over installed placards. Applying tape over placards makes them
illegible.
(a) Make sure that the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion.
(b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or
higher, to help promote good adhesion.
(c) If it is necessary to use short pieces of tape, make a minimum overlap of 0.50 in.
(12.70 mm).
(d) Push the tape firmly to make sure that there is a good bond.
NOTE: If the surface of the tape is smooth and does not have air bubbles, there is a
good bond.

E. Prepare for the Repair
SUBTASK 25-52-01-000-001
(1) If it is necessary to remove the liner for repair, do the applicable task:
(a) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal, TASK 25-52-06-000-801.
(b) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801.
(c) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal,
TASK 25-52-18-000-801.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-210-008
(2) These are the maximum damage limits for the repair of the non-honeycomb linings. These
damage limits apply to all the non-honeycomb linings (the ceiling panels and shrouds, the
sidewall linings, and the forward bulkhead in the aft cargo compartment) EXCEPT for cracks
along the contour of the ceiling shroud in the forward cargo compartment.
For cracks along the contour of the ceiling shroud in the forward cargo compartment, do this
task: Permanent Repair for the Contour of the Ceiling Shroud, TASK 25-52-01-300-808.
(a) For cracks on flat or slightly countered surfaces only:
1) Make sure that the length of the crack is not longer than 35 in. (88.9 cm).
2) Make sure that the crack is a minimum of 2 in. (5.1 cm) away from other damage
and from the panel edge on all sides.
(b) Make sure that cuts that are 36 in. (91 cm) long or less.
(c) Make sure that L-shaped tears are 9 in. (23 cm) long or less on either side.
(d) Make sure that holes are 1.5 in. (3.8 cm) in diameter or smaller.
F . Alternative 1 - Repair the Cargo Liners With Screws and a Bonded Patch
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-018
(1) Make a patch from the applicable material, sheet, G02163, or fabric, G00088.
NOTE: The sheet, G02163, or fabric, G00088, must be the same thickness as the liner where
the repair is necessary.
NOTE: Cargo areas contain sheet, G02163, and fabric, G00088. They are interchangeable.
The only difference is the fabric, G00088 is heavier and more durable. Both have the
same fire retardant value.
NOTE: The patch must make a 2 in. (51 mm) overlap on the area that is not damaged. For
example, the patch dimension that is necessary for a 1.5 in. (38 mm) diameter hole
would be 5.5 in. (140 mm) diameter.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-120-004
(2) Rub the back of the patch with abrasive cloth, B00102 (80 grit).
SUBTASK 25-52-01-120-005
(3) Use abrasive cloth, B00102 (80 grit), to remove all signs of the T edlar on the area of the liner to
be contacted by the patch.
NOTE: T edlar is the protective white layer that is on the front of the liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-007
(4) Clean all the surfaces with alcohol, B00065, or solvent, B00083, to remove the loose particles.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-019
(5) Apply adhesive, A00016, or equivalent, to the back of the patch.
25-52-01
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-020
(6) Put the patch over the center of the damaged area.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-021
(7) Apply pressure to the patch to make sure there is a good bond.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-022
(8) Attach the patch permanently with steel sheet metal screws. Install the screws approximately
1.25 in. (31.75 mm) apart and 0.60 in. (15.24 mm) from the edge of the patch.
NOTE: Put the screws in positions where they do not touch the structure that is behind the
panel.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-023
(9) Apply T ape, A50465, on the heads of the screws to keep them installed through the fiberglass
liner and patch.
(a) Make sure that the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion.
(b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or
higher, to help promote good adhesion.
G. Alternative 2 - Thermion Repair System
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-024
(1) Get the correct Thermion 9290 patch, G02393, for the shape of the damage.
NOTE: The patch must make a 2 in. (51 mm) overlap on the area that is not damaged. For
example, the patch dimension that is necessary for a 1.5 in. (38 mm) diameter hole
would be 5.5 in. (140 mm) diameter.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-120-006
(2) Rub the back of the patch with abrasive cloth, B00102 (80 grit), to remove the gloss.
(a) Be careful to not rub the impregnated scrim area.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-120-007
(3) Use abrasive, B00137 (80 grit), to remove all signs of the T edlar on the area of the liner to be
contacted by the patch.
NOTE: T edlar is the protective white layer that is on the front of the liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-008
(4) Clean all the surfaces with alcohol, B00065, or solvent, B00083, to remove the loose particles.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-025
(5) Apply EP65HT-1 adhesive, A01016, to the back of the patch and to the liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-026
(6) Put the patch over the center of the damaged area.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-027
(7) Apply pressure to the patch until the excess adhesive comes out from the edges.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-028
(8) Put T ape, A50465, around the edges of the patch.
NOTE: The tape will hold the patch while the adhesive dries (approximately 30 minutes). Also,
the tape will protect the edges of the patch when the airplane is in service.
(a) Make sure that the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion.
(b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or
higher, to help promote good adhesion.
25-52-01
H. Alternative 3 - Akro Fireguard System
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-029
(1) Get the correct Akro Fireguard repair kit, Akro Fireguard patch, A50022, for the shape of the
damage.
NOTE: The patch must make a 2 in. (51 mm) overlap on the area that is not damaged. For
example, the patch dimension that is necessary for a 1.5 in. (38 mm) diameter hole
would be 5.5 in. (140 mm) diameter.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-030
(2) Use the Akro installation instructions (in the kit) to attach the patch over the center of the
damage.
I. Alternative 4 - Gillpatch III System
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-062
(1) Get the Gillpatch III System patch, G50418, each kit has complete instructions to identify the
repairable sizes and apply the patch.
(a) The patch, G50418, must extend 2 in. (51 mm) beyond all sides of a tear or puncture.
NOTE: The patch must make a 2 in. (51 mm) overlap on the area that is not damaged.
For example, the patch dimension that is necessary for a 1.5 in. (38 mm)
diameter hole would be 5.5 in. (140 mm) diameter.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-160-015
(2) Use a lint-free clean, dry cloth and alcohol, B00065, or solvent, B00083, or equivalent, to
remove any oil, grease, dirt or stain from the damaged area to be patched.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-210-001
(3) Make sure that the area is clean and dry before you apply the patch, G50418.
(a) Wipe off any film residue that remains on the liner surface.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-210-002
(4) If there are any T edlar surface, note that it is not necessary to remove them, as the patch,
G50418, can be applied directly to T edlar.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-063
(5) When you are ready to apply the patch, G50418, peel the protective backing from the pressure
sensitive adhesive on the back of the patch, G50418.
NOTE: Handle the patch very carefully as the adhesive will adhere aggressively to any
surface that comes in contact with it.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-390-001
(6) Center the adhesive side of the patch, G50418, over the damaged area.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-390-002
(7) Use your hand to rub with circular even pressure over the entire surface of the patch, G50418,
that also includes the exposed edges.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-210-003
(8) Make sure that the patch, G50418, completely adheres to the cargo liner it covers.
(a) The patch, G50418, must be firmly stuck in place and extends 2 in. (51 mm) beyond all
sides of the tear or puncture.
J. Vertical and Sloping Sidewall Liner Edge Specific Repair
NOTE: This procedure is for the edges repair of the vertical and sloping sidewall liners with torn out
fasteners.
25-52-01
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-095
(1) If it is necessary to remove the liner for repair, do the applicable task:
(a) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal, TASK 25-52-06-000-801.
(b) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801.
(c) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal,
TASK 25-52-18-000-801.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-096
(2) Wrap the edge of the sidewall liner with 3 in. (76 mm) wide T ape, A50465.
(a) Make sure that the center of the T ape, A50465, is aligned with the edge of the sidewall
liner.
(b) Install the fastener back through the T ape, A50465.
NOTE: You can repair multiple fastener locations on the sidewall liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-097
(3) If a doubler is installed on the sidewall liner, do these steps to repair the doubler:
(a) Use a 1 in. (25 mm) wide sheet, G02163, to make a new doubler.
(b) Drill the new doubler with the hole pattern for the fasteners.
1) Make sure that the hole pattern on the new doubler is equivalent to the damaged
doubler.
(c) Attach the doubler using a doubler back Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, to the sidewall liner.
(d) Wrap the edge of the sidewall liner and doubler with 3 in. (76 mm) wide T ape, A50465.
(e) Install the fasteners to attach the doubler and sidewall liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-098
(4) If the liner was fully or partially removed, reinstall using the applicable task:
(a) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation, TASK 25-52-06-400-801.
(b) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-09-400-801.
(c) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Installation,
TASK 25-52-18-400-801.
K. Maintenance Access Panel Edge Specific Repair
NOTE: This procedure is for the edges repair of the maintenance access panels with torn out
fasteners.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-099
(1) If necessary, do the applicable task to get access to the maintenance access panel:
(a) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Removal, TASK 25-52-06-000-801.
(b) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-09-000-801.
(c) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal,
TASK 25-52-18-000-801.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-100
(2) Make sure that the doubler on the panel has no damage.
(a) If there is damage, replace the doubler with a 1 in. (25 mm) sheet, G51504.
(b) Drill the new doubler with the hole pattern for quarter-turn fasteners.
1) Make sure that the hole pattern on the new doubler is equivalent to the damage
doubler.
25-52-01
(c) Attach the doubler using a doubler back Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, to the back of the

(d) Put the retainer in its correct position with the doubler.
(e) Wrap the edge of the access panel liner and doubler with 3 in. (76 mm) wide T ape,

(c) Attach the doubler using a doubler back Nitto P-55 tape, G50885, to the access panel

(d) Wrap the edge of the access panel liner and doubler with 3 in. (76 mm) wide T ape,
A50465.
(e) Install the quarter-turn fasteners to attach the doubler and access panel liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-102
(4) If the liner was fully or partially removed, reinstall using the applicable task:
(a) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation, TASK 25-52-06-400-801.
(b) Do this task: Cargo Compartment Ceiling Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-09-400-801.
(c) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Installation,
TASK 25-52-18-400-801.

F . Cargo Lining Repair
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-005
(1) To do the structural repair on the panel, follow the SRM 51-70-06.
(a) Use fabric, G00316, soaked with resin, G50399, or resin, G50400.
1) Do not use BMS8-301.
NOTE: The structural repair is performed on one of the two, the cargo side or the non-cargo
side (fiberglass side) of the cargo liner.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-010
(2) Vacuum the bag and let the adhesive cure for a minimum of 24 hours at 77°F (25°C), or for a
minimum of 1-hour at 150°F (66°C). A minimum of 22 inches of mercury vacuum pressure
must be in operation during the cure.
NOTE: A 10 degree tolerance in each direction is approved.
(3) After the BMS8-201 (resin, G50400 or resin, G50399) repair is cured, do this task: Permanent
Repair for Flat or Slightly Curved Liners, TASK 25-52-01-340-801, or apply the AF400 patch
kit, G51353 to install a fire-resistant patch on the cargo side.
NOTE: The AF400 patch kit, G51353 is the only fire-resistant patch approved for contoured
repair areas.

F . Repair the Contour with a Steel Patch
SUBTASK 25-52-01-000-004
(1) Remove the damaged areas.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-011
(2) Fabricate a repair patch from CRES sheet 0.050 in. (0.13 cm) thick manufactured from
stainless steel sheet, G51187, stainless steel sheet, G51188, or stainless steel sheet, G51189.
25-52-01
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-012
(3) Use adhesive, A01076 to bond the stainless steel sheet, G51189 patch to the ceiling shroud.
NOTE: : An optional method to bond the patch is to use seal, G02186 tape to install the patch
to the ceiling shroud.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-013
(4) Attach the patch permanently with screws. Use BACS12FA3K* screws, NAS1149D0363J
washers and BACN10JC3CD nuts or equivalent.
(a) Fastener spacing in the forward-aft direction is 4.0 in. (101.6 mm) typical.
(b) Install two rows of fasteners past the end of the damage.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-014
(5) Drill holes for the bolts around the edge of the patch. Drill the holes with a maximum of 4.0 in.
(101.6 mm) of separation, and approximately 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) from the edges of the stainless
steel patch. Make sure that the holes go through the patch and the original panel.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-200-002
(6) Make sure that there is sufficient clearance between the screws and the adjacent structure and
systems behind the panel.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-420-008
(7) Install the screws, nuts and washers.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-410-003
(8) Apply Nitto P-629 tape, G50428, over the fasteners and the joint edge to keep them installed
through the patch.
(a) Make sure the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion.
(b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or
higher, to help promote good adhesion.
G. Repair the Contour with a Preformed Patch
SUBTASK 25-52-01-300-003
(1) Make a patch from the applicable material fabric, G02312. The patch can be made from 4 plies
of the fabric, G02312 material.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-340-002
(2) Do these steps to fabricate or laminate the preformed patch:
(a) Make sure that the radius of the preformed patch matches the panel radius.
(b) Build a laminate equal in thickness to the number of plies removed.
(c) T aper sand this laminate to fit the plies removed from the panel.
(d) If you need to splice prepreg plies, overlap splices are preferred.
1) Make sure that overlap widths are between 0.13 in. (3.30 mm) and 1.25 in.
(31.75 mm) wide.
2) Make sure that lap splices in adjacent plies are staggered.
(e) You can use butt splices for laminates or panels that have four or more plies on each
side.
1) Make sure that overlaps are not more than 0.01 in. (0.25 mm).
2) Make sure that the maximum gap between prepreg edges are not more than
0.02 in. (0.51 mm).
3) Make sure that butt splices on adjacent plies are staggered.
25-52-01
SUBTASK 25-52-01-350-001
(3) Use adhesive, A01076 to bond the fabric, G02312 patch to the ceiling shroud.
NOTE: An optional method to bond the patch is to use seal, G02186 tape to install the patch
to the ceiling shroud.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-420-001
(4) Install the fasteners as necessary.
(a) Fastener spacing in the forward-aft direction is 4.0 in. (101.6 mm) typical.
(b) Install two rows of fasteners past the end of the damage.
SUBTASK 25-52-01-350-002
(5) Apply Nitto P-629 tape, G50428, over the fasteners and the joint edge to keep them installed
through the patch.
(a) Make sure that the tape is within shelf life limits for optimum tape adhesion.
(b) Where possible, apply the tape to warm surfaces that are approximately 60°F (16°C) or
higher, to help promote good adhesion.

6. Neoprene Coated Cargo Liner Repair
A. General
(1) This task gives instructions to repair the neoprene-coated fiberglass liners in the lower lobe
cargo compartments.
(2) There are two repair alternatives. It is only necessary to do one of the repairs that follow:
(a) Repair the neoprene-coated liners with mechanical fasteners.
(b) Repair the neoprene-coated liner with fiberglass thread, G01498.
(3) Liners designed for blow out if decompression occurs are not repairable and should be
replaced.
(4) Refer to this procedure for cargo liner damage limits: CARGO COMPARTMENT -
INSPECTION/CHECK, PAGEBLOCK 25-52-00/601.
